kurz: Why deviations from the market portfolio call for a fixed upper limit and a written record more than for a better opinion.

bloecke.md:
A portfolio with a **core-satellite structure** consists of two parts with different purposes. The core is a portfolio that would be complete even without anything else, that is, one or two broad, low-cost index funds held without any opinion on the state of the market. The satellite is the deliberate deviation from it, for example a sector, a region, a factor, a handful of individual shares or gold. More important than the mix is the asymmetry between the two parts. The satellite depends on the core, because the core carries the result while the thesis is being tested. The core, on the other hand, does not need the satellite.

The structure thus serves to limit damage and is not a concept for increasing returns. It does not answer the question of how to beat the market. It answers the more practical question of how much the attempt may cost without your retirement provision depending on it.

A satellite is based on a thesis; it does not serve diversification. Investors should be able to say in one sentence what they are betting against and how they would notice that they were wrong. If they cannot, the satellite is merely a second core holding with higher costs.

## The base rate of active funds

Morningstar's Active/Passive Barometer compares active funds with the cost-adjusted average of index funds in the same category, that is, with an alternative that can actually be bought and not with an index. For European equity funds, the ten-year success rate in the first half of 2026 was 11.9%. Funds count as successful if they survive and outperform. According to the SPIVA analysis by S&P Dow Jones Indices, 98.2% of euro-denominated global equity funds lagged behind their benchmark over ten years (as of June 2025).

These results were achieved by full-time teams with Bloomberg terminals, access to analysts and company visits. The same distribution of outcomes applies to a private satellite, only with fewer resources. Nevertheless, a strict ban is often the worse advice in practice. Investors who want to give it a try and have no designated place for it will at some point try it with the core. The **satellite budget** therefore gives deviations a fixed place with an upper limit; its purpose is to limit them, not to permit them.

bloecke.unter: Morningstar Active/Passive Barometer, Europe, as of the first half of 2026. The longer the period, the smaller the share of funds that survive and outperform, and every satellite has to be measured against this base rate.

bloecke.md:
## Return contribution of a satellite

A satellite's contribution to the portfolio result is the product of its weight and its lead over the investment that would otherwise have been held in the same place. The lead is therefore always measured against the core, because the core was the alternative, and not against zero.

bloecke.formel: Return contribution = Satellite allocation × (Satellite return − Core return)
bloecke.erklaerung: The benchmark is the core and not zero. A satellite that returned 8% while the core returned 10% has cost money, even though it shows a gain.
variablen: share of the total portfolio, not of the equity portion
opportunity cost: what the money would otherwise have earned
bloecke.beispiel: With a satellite allocation of 10% and a lead of four percentage points a year, the contribution is 0.4 percentage points. A portfolio return of 6.0% becomes 6.4%.

bloecke.titel: Contribution to portfolio return in percentage points a year
bloecke.unter: Calculated as allocation times lead, not a forecast. A satellite with a 10% weight and a lead of ten points shifts the portfolio return by one point; with a shortfall of ten points, the same calculation applies downwards.

bloecke.md: The table shows a dilemma. An allocation that is small enough to be harmless is also too small to change the result noticeably. A satellite that is large enough to change the result noticeably is no longer a satellite. It is then a second core portfolio without the core's diversification. It makes sense to book the budget as the cost of learning and as limited room for your own ideas, not as a source of return, and to set your expectations accordingly.

On top of the selection decision comes the decision about timing. Morningstar's 2026 study “Mind the Gap” compares the return of funds with the return of the investors in these funds for the decade to the end of 2025. The funds achieved 9.9% a year, the investors 8.7%. The gap of 1.2 percentage points arises solely from the timing of purchases and sales. It is unevenly distributed. In the calmest fifth of funds it is 0.4 points, in the most volatile fifth over 2 points, for international equity ETFs 2.5 and for crypto ETFs since 2024 around 14 points. It is therefore largest in the areas from which satellites usually come.

## Shift from core to satellite

This shift rarely comes about through a single big decision. Usually three inconspicuous mechanisms are at work.

The first is the monthly contribution. An investor who aims for a satellite allocation of 10% but directs 20% of the monthly contribution into the satellite has already abandoned the allocation. With equal returns, the composition of the portfolio converges over the long term on the composition of the contributions. The allocation is therefore decided by the standing order and not by the split in the portfolio.

The second is buying more. A satellite that loses 40% shrinks from a weight of 10% to 6.25% if the core is unchanged. If the core's rebalancing logic is applied symmetrically, this results in a buy order. Money then flows from the core into a thesis that is currently being disproved. Satellites are therefore subject to an asymmetric rule. The allocation is an upper limit and not a target: above the limit, the position is capped; below it, nothing happens.

The third is attention. A 5% share of the portfolio can take up 95% of the time you spend on the portfolio. This is the predictable result of only the satellite having a story, and not a character flaw. Costs arise when this attention leads to interventions in the core.

punkte: Satellite allocation as an upper limit, not a target
Only new money flows into the satellite, never proceeds from the core
Fixed capping of everything that grows above the limit
No top-ups after losses; the loss stays as it is
Separate securities account or sub-account so that the allocation can be read off

rechts.titel: Habits at the expense of the core
punkte: Savings plan share higher than the target allocation
“Averaging down” because getting in now looks cheaper
Raising the upper limit because the satellite is doing well at the moment
Applying rebalancing symmetrically to the satellite
No fixed date for reviewing the thesis

bloecke.md:
## Tax consequences in Germany

A satellite is switched more often than the core, and every switch brings the tax forward in time. Realised gains are subject to 25% flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer) plus solidarity surcharge, 26.375% in total, and correspondingly more with church tax. For equity funds, the 30% [[Partial exemption (Teilfreistellung)|partial exemption (Teilfreistellung)]] under Section 20 InvStG (Investment Tax Act) reduces the tax base, so that the effective tax is then 18.46% of the gain. Individual shares have no partial exemption; the full 26.375% applies to them. Investors cannot decide for themselves which units count as sold in a partial sale. The first-in, first-out principle under Section 20(4) sentence 7 EStG (Income Tax Act) is decisive. Under this principle, the oldest units are always deemed to have been sold first, and these are usually the ones with the highest gain.

For individual share satellites, there is an additional restriction on loss offsetting. Losses from the sale of shares may only be offset against gains from share sales (Section 20(6) sentence 4 EStG). They are collected in a separate loss offset pot and can remain unused there for years, while gains from the ETF core are taxed in full. The saver's allowance (Sparerpauschbetrag) of €1,000, or €2,000 for joint assessment (Section 20(9) EStG), only eases the burden at the beginning. In a growing portfolio, it is used up anyway by distributions and the [[Advance lump sum (Vorabpauschale)|advance lump sum (Vorabpauschale)]].

Investors also do not always determine the timing of realisation themselves. Niche funds with assets of less than about €50 million to €100 million are hardly profitable for the provider. If such a fund is liquidated, the units are compulsorily sold at the redemption price, and the gain becomes taxable regardless of your own tax planning. Of the thematic funds that Morningstar tracked over fifteen years to mid-2024, 45% still existed at the end.

Two portfolios of €15,000 each both earn 6% a year before tax over twenty years; the saver's allowance has already been used up elsewhere.

The first portfolio follows buy and hold. The final value before tax is €48,107, the gain €33,107. After the 30% partial exemption, €23,175 is taxable, the tax is €6,112, and €41,995 remains net.

In the second portfolio, the money is switched into the next idea every two years. In each round, the value rises by 12.36%, of which 18.46% goes to the tax authorities. The net factor per round is 1.1008 instead of 1.1236. After ten rounds, the portfolio stands at €39,183.

The difference is €2,812, even though no selection decision was worse. Expressed as an after-tax return, this is around 0.36 percentage points a year. To make up for this shortfall, the satellite has to earn around 0.44 percentage points a year more before tax purely because of the switching. For individual shares without a partial exemption, it is around 0.49 points after tax and around 0.66 points before tax. Advance lump sums are left out in both cases; they reduce the lead of the untouched portfolio slightly without reversing it.

bloecke.md:
## Written documentation

What distinguishes a satellite from a spontaneous trade is that it is recorded in writing. Without a note, after three years you no longer know why the position was bought, and you invent a reason after the fact that fits the current price. Five lines per satellite are enough: date and amount, the thesis in one sentence, the event that would disprove the thesis, the upper limit as a percentage and in euros, and the date of the review.

In the evaluation, what counts is the comparison with the core over the same period, weighted by the money invested. Whether the position shows a gain is irrelevant for this. If the balance over three to five years and across all satellites is negative, the budget should be reduced or scrapped instead of trying out another satellite. Of all the parts of the structure, only the record turns an opinion into an experiment.

schritte.text: As a percentage and in euros, relative to total wealth including instant-access savings, and before there is a specific idea.
The satellite is funded exclusively from new money. Selling core units to finance it is ruled out, because it triggers tax and reverses the structure.

schritte.titel: Write down the thesis and stopping criterion
schritte.text: One sentence on why the market is supposedly wrong here, and one sentence on how the opposite would become apparent. Without the second sentence, nothing is bought.
Above the upper limit, the position is cut back to the allocation; below it, nothing happens. Note the date of the review at the same time.
Compare the satellite return with the core return, set the tax attributable to the satellites from the contract notes alongside it and write the result under the old note.

bloecke.md: A separate securities account or sub-account for the satellites costs nothing and has three advantages. The allocation can be read off without any calculation, the satellites appear in their own account statements, and the most eye-catching position does not dominate your view of the core every day. You only get a separate tax certificate if the satellite account is held at a second bank. At the same bank, the institution offsets gains and losses across all of a customer's securities accounts and issues a joint tax certificate (Section 43a(3) EStG). With two banks, losses at one are only offset against gains at the other via the tax return; for this, a loss certificate (Verlustbescheinigung) has to be requested by 15 December.

A satellite is out of the question as long as the emergency fund is not in place, consumer debts are outstanding or the money will be needed in less than five years. In these cases, the question of deviating from the core does not yet arise, because the core has to be built first.

Suppose that after three good years, 10% has become 22%. A single thesis then determines the portfolio result. Capping feels wrong in this situation, because you are selling your best position and paying tax on it. That is why the rule is written down beforehand and not only once you are in this situation.

Two approaches are justifiable. In the first, the position is cut back to the allocation, the tax is paid and the proceeds are put into the core. The second is **passive dilution**. Nothing is sold, but every new euro flows into the core until the weight is right again. This approach saves tax but takes years and only works with a monthly contribution that is high relative to the portfolio. It is not justifiable to raise the upper limit after the fact because the price has risen. Such an increase says nothing new about the thesis, but it does say something about how you handle success.

mitnehmen: The core must be complete even without the satellite; otherwise it is a concentrated portfolio that is a core-satellite structure in name only.
A satellite's return contribution is its allocation times its lead over the core, and at realistic allocations it amounts to only a fraction of a percentage point, upwards as well as downwards.
The allocation is an upper limit and not a target, so above the limit the position is capped, below it nothing is done, and there are never any top-ups.

Frequent switching costs return even without a bad pick, because FIFO and flat-rate withholding tax end tax deferral: in the model, around 0.36 percentage points of after-tax return a year for funds and around 0.49 for individual shares.
Without a written thesis, stopping criterion and annual review date, the satellite cannot be evaluated and is therefore never ended.

begriffe.text: Portfolio structure consisting of a broadly diversified, low-cost core and clearly limited deviations. Even without satellites, the core must be a complete portfolio.
Upper limit for all active deviations, set in advance as a percentage of total wealth and in euros. Above the limit, positions are capped; below it, they are not topped up.
Reducing a position that has grown too large without selling, by directing new contributions exclusively into the core until the weight is right again. The method avoids tax but takes time.
Separate pot for losses from share sales under Section 20(6) sentence 4 EStG. Such losses can only be offset against gains from share sales, not against fund income or interest income.
